title: add-jsonschema-strict-response-format-openai-compat
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Add first-class JSON Schema response_format support with a strict validation mode and OpenAI-compat error shapes. This PR implements schema-aware streaming enforcement, clearer validation errors for downstream SDKs and the OpenAI compatibility layer, and docs/examples for migrating from ad-hoc structured-output approaches.

Summary of changes and goals: - Implement response_format: { type: "json_schema", schema: ... , strict: boolean } on the Redwood API surface. - Add a strict validation path that fails fast for streaming and non-streaming responses, returning standardized error objects compatible with OpenAI-style schema error shapes. - Ensure streaming stability by verifying incremental JSON fragments against the schema where possible and falling back to graceful fallback policies on divergence. - Surface improved error messages with a stable error_code enum so SDKs and client-side code can reliably handle validation failures. - Add end-to-end tests, unit tests for schema canonicalization, and examples in docs. - Maintain backward compatibility: default behavior remains permissive unless strict: true is requested.

Checklist: - [x] API surface + request/response contract defined and documented - [x] Runtime enforcement for strict mode (sync + streaming paths) - [x] OpenAI-compat error mapping implemented - [x] E2E tests covering streaming and non-streaming strict failures - [x] Integration tests for SDKs (TS/Python) - [x] Docs and migration guide added

Design notes: The implementation introduces a small schema canonicalizer to avoid flaky mismatches from ordering/metadata. For streaming, we attempt incremental validation using a tolerant SAX-style validator: when strict=true we abort the stream and emit a well-formed validation error as a final chunk; when strict=false we attach validation warnings to the response metadata. The OpenAI compatibility layer maps our internal ValidationError -> { type: "invalid_response", code: "response_schema_mismatch", message: string, details: string }.

Compatibility: Default behavior is unchanged. Customers who opt in to response_format.json_schema and strict=true will see deterministic failures for invalid outputs. SDKs were updated to recognize the compat error shape and expose a typed exception. Migration docs include examples for function-calling + structured output combos.

Related: Linear ENG-2345 (schema strict mode), ENG-2987 (streaming validator), SUP-1023 (customer reported flakiness for function-calling + structured outputs).

Introduce incremental JSON Schema validator used by streaming and batch paths
Map internal validation errors to OpenAI-compatible shapes for SDKs

release_notes: Added support for response_format=\"json_schema\" with an optional strict=true flag. When strict=true, responses that do not conform to the provided JSON Schema will cause a deterministic validation error. Streaming responses will be aborted with a standardized error chunk (OpenAI-compatible error shape). Default behavior remains permissive.
user_facing_examples: Error (compat): { \"type\": \"invalid_response\", \"code\": \"response_schema_mismatch\", \"message\": \"Output does not match schema: missing required property 'user_id'\", \"details\": \"path: \"/user_id\"; expected integer; got null\" }
